meridian.hint: Reach the camp, and find out whose grave is in the sewn tent.

perimeter.text: A ring of canvas tents stands around a rectangle of broken glass lying flat in the dirt: the floor of an observation gallery, with no gallery around it. Eleven cots. A kettle on a cold stove is warm. No one is here, and every tent flap is tied back, as if for someone expected.

text_by_lens.machine: A field station, abandoned mid-shift: eleven cots, instrument stakes at even intervals, a kettle still warm. Someone should be logging this.
text_by_lens.ritual: A camp laid out as a circle, tents facing inward to the glass. The dirt between them is worn into a path by bare feet.
text_by_lens.resonance: The tents stand on the nodes of a standing wave. You can feel where the glass floor hums and where it doesn't.
text_by_lens.prison: A cordon. Every tent faces the glass, every stake points at it. They were not studying it. They were watching it.
text_by_lens.mirror: Eleven cots. Twelve. Eleven. The kettle was warm before you got here, and it is warm because you got here.

choices.label: Log the instruments staked round the perimeter before you cross it.
Walk the ring of tents once, in the footprints already worn into it.
Cross where the hum is loudest. That is where they would have stood.
Go in through the cut in the fence. It was cut from the inside.

camp_center.text: You stand on the glass floor. Under it, very far down, there is a room where eleven people are looking up at you. The tents around you hold what they left: a survey tent, a sleeping tent, and a tent with its flap sewn shut.

choices.label: Palpate the sewn-shut flap with the Dirty Glove before you cut it.

survey_tent.text: Folding tables, a theodolite aimed straight down, and a roll of five tuning forks that do not match. They hum when you pick them up. They go on humming after you put them in your pack.

choices.label: Look in the tent with its flap sewn shut.

sleeping_tent.text: Eleven sleeping bags, zipped, empty, each shaped around a body that is not there. At the foot of the twelfth stands a pendulum on a rigid rod, rising from the floor, leaning toward the survey tent.

choices.label: Look in the tent with its flap sewn shut.

sewn_tent.text: Inside is a grave pile: stones, a boot, a water bottle. It is yours. It is still warm. Someone has scratched a note into the bottle: the roster is in the gallery, and you are already on it.

text_by_lens.machine: A cairn over a supply cache, marked with your survivor number. A clerical error, surely.
text_by_lens.ritual: A grave dressed with care: stones, a boot, a bottle. Someone mourned you before you arrived.
text_by_lens.resonance: A grave pile, and the stones in it are arranged in the figure the nodes make on the map.
text_by_lens.prison: A grave pile, sealed from the inside. Whatever was put down here tried to get out through the bottle.
text_by_lens.mirror: It is your grave pile. It is warm. You check your pulse, and it is slower than it should be.

log_disagrees.text: Every instrument reads the same number, and the number is your name. You lose your nerve and the light.

ring_tightens.text: The ring of footprints is smaller on the second half of the circuit. You come out where you went in.

hum_takes_hold.text: The hum gets into your teeth and holds. When it lets go you are back at the perimeter, and the sun has moved.

fence_remembers.text: The cut wire closes behind you, then in front of you. You back out the way you came.

scrap_recounts.text: You count the scrap on the table three times and get three numbers. You leave with the smallest.

radio_early.text: A radio in the bedding says what you will say next, a second before you say it. You stop talking. You stop searching.

glove_chooses.text: The glove chooses where to press, and it chooses wrong. Something on the other side of the canvas presses back.

grave_pile.text: The stitches come apart on their own before you touch them. You do not go in. Not this time.
